findings.claim: The decimal formatter now passes StandardFormat('F') with no precision to Utf8Formatter.TryFormat. For 'F', Utf8Formatter defaults to 2 fractional digits, so serialized decimals are rounded. For example, 1.2345m is written as "1.23" and 0.001m as "0.00", which deserializes to 0. Scale also changes: 1.5m is written as "1.50" instead of "1.5". This silently corrupts data. The change is unrelated to REQ-2297 and alters the wire format.

receipt_plan.detail: Run Receipts.GeneratedTests.DecimalFormatPrecisionTests.DecimalRoundTripsExactly("1.2345" / "0.001") and DecimalPreservesScale. These serialize with MessagePackSerializer and deserialize back. On head they produce 1.23, 0 and "1.50". A byte-diff of Serialize(1.2345m) between base and head would also show "1.2345" vs "1.23".

findings.claim: The resolver templates now put [ExcludeFromCodeCoverage] on the user's own `partial class` (the [GeneratedMessagePackResolver] / [CompositeResolver] type). ExcludeFromCodeCoverageAttribute has AllowMultiple=false. A user who already annotated their resolver partial with [ExcludeFromCodeCoverage], the obvious workaround before this change, now gets CS0579 (duplicate attribute), and the project stops compiling.

receipt_plan.detail: Run Receipts.GeneratedTests.ExcludeFromCodeCoverageDuplicateTests.UserAnnotatedGeneratedResolverStillCompiles and UserAnnotatedCompositeResolverStillCompiles. On head the generated resolver output produces CS0579 'Duplicate ExcludeFromCodeCoverage attribute'.

findings.claim: The attribute is wrapped in `#if !NETSTANDARD2_0 && !NETFRAMEWORK`, so it is omitted for consumers targeting netstandard2.0 and every .NET Framework TFM. ExcludeFromCodeCoverageAttribute exists in both (.NET Framework 4.0+ mscorlib, netstandard2.0) and is valid on classes there. Generated code compiled for those targets is still not excluded from coverage, so 'All generated code is decorated' is not met for a large share of users.

receipt_plan.detail: Drive CSharpGeneratorDriver over a [MessagePackObject] type plus a [GeneratedMessagePackResolver] partial, with CSharpParseOptions.WithPreprocessorSymbols("NETSTANDARD2_0") (and separately "NETFRAMEWORK"). Then call RunGeneratorsAndUpdateCompilation and assert the generated formatter's INamedTypeSymbol.GetAttributes() contains System.Diagnostics.CodeAnalysis.ExcludeFromCodeCoverageAttribute. It is absent on head.

findings.claim: Because the attribute is applied to the user-declared partial resolver class rather than only to generator-owned types, it also excludes from coverage any members the user hand-writes in their own part of that class.

receipt_plan.detail: CompositeResolverTemplate.tt:7-10 and ResolverTemplate.tt:14-17 emit the attribute on `partial class <#= ResolverName.Name #>`, which is the user's own type. Attributes on any partial declaration apply to the whole type.
